Dialogs.Dialog: Kobayakawa
Don't you think a lot of people have been forgetting to return library books lately？
Have they...？
You haven't noticed？ Are you even taking your library duty seriously？
I am. I show up when I'm supposed to, don't I？
Just showing up isn't enough, you know.
Anyway, are that many people really forgetting to return them？
Yeah. For the regulars who come in a lot, I try to drop a hint and remind them, but...
I see. At this rate, we're just going to keep losing books.
Right! There's nothing more disappointing than going to borrow a book you want and finding out it's not there.
Alright, I'll try to think of something we can do, too.
Yeah. Thanks.
Kobayakawa
▲主人公＊▲. Yesterday I went to the classroom of someone with an overdue book.
You're really dedicated to the job.
Well, you're never around when it actually counts.
...Sorry. So how did it go？ You got it back, right？
Yeah, I got it back. But the person who had it was a total jerk.
Wait, did they do something to you？
Hmm. So you actually do worry about me？
...Of course I do.
Thanks. I'm fine, though. They just made a snide remark.
Giving me that 'I was gonna return it today' excuse... Like, quit lying already.
Maybe we should figure out a way to get people to be more mindful when they borrow books？
Yeah, maybe you're right.
Kobayakawa
Hey, about those people who keep forgetting to return their books.
Did you go track them down by yourself again？
Yeah. But there's just no end to it.
A lot of them probably forgot they even borrowed a book in the first place.
They don't seem to realize that library books belong to everyone.
Well, I say that, but I once borrowed a book and completely forgot about it for ages...
Ow.
You're disqualified from the library committee.
Then how about putting up posters or something as a reminder？ If the whole school sees them, some people should remember they still have books out, right？
...Oh. That might actually work. I'll try bringing it up with the upperclassmen.
Kobayakawa
Hey, remember how you suggested making posters the other day？
I talked it over with the upperclassmen, and we put up some simple ones in the hallway for now.
Yeah, I saw them. The ones posted right by the library entrance, right？
Right there.
So, is it working...？
Actually, it seems like even just that is making a big difference.
There was a whole line at the return counter after school.
I see. That's great. Guess that solves the problem, then.
It's not that simple. It might only work for now, anyway.
I see. You're really dedicated to your job, ▲小早川＊▲.
Don't be dumb. I'm just doing what I'm supposed to. Still...
Maybe I'll work even harder so you'll praise me some more... Hehe.
Kobayakawa
A girl in my class brought in homemade cookies the other day.
Baking sweets is a pretty girly hobby.
Yeah, but all the boys were fawning over her. It was painful to watch.
Even our homeroom teacher was happily eating them. The world really is coming to an end.
Your homeroom teacher's a guy, right？ That's just how guys are, so cut them some slack.
They're just cookies, you know？ Anyone can make those.
It's less about the taste and more about the fact that they're homemade.
Hmm. So you're into that type of girl too？
Especially when she's not great at it, but still tries her hardest to make them.
...Why are you looking at me like that？ I can bake cookies, you know.
Kobayakawa
About that girl who brought in cookies the other day...
Yeah. I bet she's really popular with the boys now.
Nope. She's actually popular with the girls.
Why？
All the girls want her to teach them how to bake. And I mean, they really were good.
Huh. That's an unexpected turn of events.
Right？ Apparently they're going to her house after school soon to bake together.
Apparently？ So you're not going, ▲小早川＊▲.
...Yeah. That's just not really my thing, you know？
That's a shame. I really wanted to try cookies you made, ▲小早川＊▲.
...Oh. Okay.
Kobayakawa
Hey, so I ended up joining that baking group.
Huh？ Didn't you say last time that you weren't going？
It'd be weird if I was the only one in class who didn't go.
(The old ▲小早川＊▲ never would've gone, though...)
What？
I was just thinking how much I'm looking forward to your cookies, ▲小早川＊▲.
I never said I was giving any to you.
Really！？
...Oh, fine. If I mess any up, I'll bring them to you.
Come on, bring me the ones that actually turn out good.
I'll think about it.
Kobayakawa
Here. I went to that baking group.
Going by the look on your face, they turned out well. Oh, you even wrapped them up. They look delicious.
...You haven't even opened it yet. Don't just say stuff like that.
Fair point. Alright, let's see how they taste...
...They're really good.
Why do you have to look so surprised？
Because these are good enough to be sold in a store.
Hehe. Wonder what kind of cookies I should bake next, then.
...Wait, cookies again？ What about something else？
Nothing else. Cookies are all I know how to make.
Kobayakawa
You know that empty lot behind the school？
Yeah. That overgrown place full of bushes, right？
Yeah. Someone abandoned a kitten there.
An abandoned cat, huh. You hear about it a lot lately, but it's awful.
Right？ I don't get how anyone could have the nerve to abandon something so cute.
The owner probably had their reasons, but they didn't have to abandon it.
So I was thinking of secretly keeping it at school.
Is that a good idea？ A teacher's gonna find out.
They already did.
I knew it. So what happened？
I tucked the kitten under my arm and ran all over school...
In the end, the teacher gave in and agreed to help find it a home. The end.
Don't give me 'the end'...
Kobayakawa
They found someone to take in that stray kitten.
Oh yeah？ That's great.
...Yeah.
You don't seem too happy about it？
Just, having it leave me... It's still so little.
Why not ask if you can visit and pet it at the new owner's house？
If I do that, I'll get too attached and won't be able to let go.
I see... Then all we can do is pray from afar that the kitten has a happy life.
...Yeah. That's what's best for the little one, too.
Kobayakawa
I heard from the teacher about that kitten. They said it's sick right now.
Eh！？
Apparently the owner who abandoned it didn't even get it properly vaccinated.
That's awful... How bad is it？
...Not good, apparently.
If something happens to it... What am I gonna do？
Hang in there. You've gotta believe in the little guy, ▲小早川＊▲.
...Yeah.
It'll be okay. A vet is taking proper care of it now.
Yeah... you're right. I'll root for it, even if it's from afar.
Kobayakawa
There really is a cat god in this world. Definitely!!
？ Oh, I get it. That kitten pulled through, huh.
Yeah. Maybe my prayers reached the cat god.
Maybe so.
And also... hehe.
There's more？
The owner gave me a photo of it all better now. Seriously... it's SO cute.
I really want a cat... Though I can't right now.
Well, hopefully in the future you can live surrounded by lots of cats.
The future, huh...
Hm？ What is it？
Hehe, I'm counting on you, okay？
Kobayakawa
Hey, question. What kind of books have you been reading lately？
Books, huh... I haven't been reading much lately.
You fail as a library committee member.
What about you, ▲小早川＊▲？ Reading anything？
German literature lately. Like 'Young Heinter's Sorrows.'
German literature, huh... What's that one about again？
It's about a young man who falls into despair over his unrequited first love.
I'll lend it to you when I'm done.
...I'd really rather not fall into despair, though.
Kobayakawa
You look pretty grim. What's wrong？
This story's heavier than I expected.
Oh, right. 'Young Heinter's Sorrows,' was it？
The main character is a young man who falls in love with a beautiful woman who's already engaged.
His feelings are never returned, so he ends up despairing over everything and kills himself.
...That's a tragedy.
Hey. What do you think about love that has zero chance of working out？
I wouldn't want to go through it, and I can't even imagine it.
I see. Smooth sailing all the way for you, huh.
I wouldn't say smooth sailing, but my love did work out.
...What are you even saying, idiot.
Hey. Still reading that book？ Young Heinter's...
Kobayakawa
Sorrows. Just a little left, though. The more I read, the more hopeless it gets.
Come to think of it, I heard when it first came out, some young people fell into despair and killed themselves the same way.
They should've just blown off some steam with a fighting game before letting it get to them that badly.
Pretty sure they didn't have fighting games back then...
What if... I fell so deep into despair that I got sick of everything？ What would you do...？
There's no way you'd fall into despair.
You don't know that.
I told you I'm on your side till the very end, didn't I？ You won't fall into despair.
Quit trying to act cool... Hehe.
Kobayakawa
Haaah...
Short on sleep？
Yeah. I stayed up all night and finished the rest in one go.
Oh, that Young-something book. Was it good？
Are you planning to just hear my thoughts and pretend you read it？
...Caught me, huh.
If you're curious, read it yourself.
...Sounds like a tough read, though. Having to sit through endless tragedy sounds rough, too.
The story uses that tragedy to ask the philosophical question of how to live.
Hmm. That's one philosophy I'd rather go my whole life without understanding.
Well, normally, yeah. Nobody chooses to live a tragic life...
Right, right. Love is way more fun and fulfilling when it actually works out.
...What are you grinning to yourself about？ Idiot.
Kobayakawa
Hey. Have you heard the rumors about the new fast-food place opening up？
No, I haven't. They're opening a new place？
Yeah. Apparently they're hiring part-timers right now.
That alone is enough to get people talking, huh.
They say the uniform is really cute.
Huh.
Not really interested？
Not in the uniform itself.
Hmm. Well, what if I said I wanted to wear that uniform？
It was a joke. Stop picturing it already.
Kobayakawa
About that fast-food place I mentioned the other day.
Oh, the one rumored to have the cute uniforms？
Yeah. It really was cute.
Did you go all the way out there to see it？
As if. One of the boys brought back a flyer.
So, how was it...？
It's not quite my taste, I think.
How so？ Waitress uniforms can't be all that different, right？
Well... I want it to have a little more edge to it, not just be cute.
And have punk music blasting inside the restaurant.
Doesn't sound like a very relaxing place to eat...
You think？ Sounds like the ideal place to me...
Kobayakawa
Do you know Ms. Kawamura？
The newlywed teacher, right？ She's really pretty, and when news of her marriage got out, a lot of guys cried...
Boys... What a bunch of idiots.
...What about Ms. Kawamura？
I heard she's going on maternity leave starting this month.
Oh, wow. So she's having a baby.
Yeah. All the girls are making a fuss right now over which parent the baby's going to look like.
Getting a little ahead of themselves, aren't they？ Her husband's built like a rock, right？
Yeah. She showed me a photo once, and they really are Beauty and the Beast.
I wonder how the two of us look to other people.
Are you calling me a beast？
Who knows？ You're definitely not a prince on a white horse, at least.
...I can't argue with that.
Well, I prefer a charming beast over a prince anyway.
Kobayakawa
Hey. Is raising a baby really that hard？
Everyone's saying Ms. Kawamura might not come back to work because childcare is so tough.
She's popular and a good teacher, so it'd be a shame if that's true.
Right？ Though I can kind of see how raising a kid would be rough.
Do you have experience raising kids or something, ▲小早川＊▲？
...Obviously not.
W-what's with that look？ I just figured maybe you'd babysat a relative's kid or something.
Oh, right. ...You know I have a little brother at home, right？
Now that you mention it, yeah.
He's usually cute and easy to handle, but once he starts crying, it's a nightmare. Like a little monster.
A newborn baby must be even harder to deal with.
Yeah. I hope she doesn't quit, if possible, but you can't really blame her if she does.
Kobayakawa
...This is the worst. Biggest crisis of my life.
What on earth happened？
I got stuck giving a speech in the next English class.
Doesn't that mean you were specially chosen for it？
People know I'm into Western music, so...
Ah, so that's why.
Listening to it and speaking it are two totally different things, you know.
Still, it's already decided, right？
...You're on my side here, right？
I can help you prep, sure, but you're on your own for the actual speech.
...Yep, the absolute worst.
By the way, how did that English speech go？
Kobayakawa
...It's over.
Then tell me how it went. I was wondering about it.
Yeah. Not bad... I think. The teacher praised me, at least.
Hey, that's great. What did you talk about？
I quoted some Killer Bambis lyrics and talked about the world of their music...
Give me the short version.
Basically, how much I love Killer Bambis. The words just flow when it's something you like.
I can picture that. You really get going when you talk about how much you love cats, too, ▲小早川＊▲.
Okay then, let's hear you talk about how much you love me right now.
...How did we jump to that？
I see... So you don't really like me that much.
Come on, why here of all places...
Boo-hoo-hoo...
(Her speech might've gone well, but her acting is terrible...)
Kobayakawa
The girls on the library committee decided to hold a reading session.
A reading session？ Like everyone getting together to read books？
Not quite. We're volunteering to read books to preschoolers.
Nobody told us about that？
Yeah. It's just the girls for now.
Huh. I didn't think you'd take part in that kind of thing, ▲小早川＊▲.
That's an unfair assumption. It's fun thinking about what books little kids will enjoy.
Come to think of it, you read to your little brother at home, right？
Seeing him listen with his eyes all lit up makes me happy too.
Plus, if it gets kids to love books, that's a great thing.
Yeah. This might actually be a pretty big responsibility.
Kobayakawa
That reading session the other day went over pretty well.
Oh yeah？ That's great. What kind of book did you read them？
I figured a short picture book would be good to start with, so I picked "The Fox Goes Shopping."
Never heard of it. What's it about？
A little fox goes shopping for the first time and has all kinds of adventures. The boys especially loved it.
Even the teachers and moms asked me to come back and do it again next time. Hehe.
Maybe you're cut out to be a preschool teacher, ▲小早川＊▲.
You think so？ Though it really surprised me how precocious kids are these days.
Precocious？
They asked, "Do you have a boyfriend？" And that was coming from a four-year-old couple.
Four years old, huh... So what did you tell them？
I told them I'd show them a photo of my boyfriend next time I visit. Hehe, hope you're ready.
(Somehow that makes me kind of nervous...)
